members.title: Preserve the exclusion reason when no independent verifier remains
members.detail: The exclusion error is emitted only when the filtered roster is empty. If the remaining allowed verifier raised the candidate, pickVerifier throws a self-verification error and discards the origin exclusion reason. Reproduced with a temporary copy of the panel integration test using verifier targets ["delta/m", "alpha/m"]. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun test --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-panel.test.ts". Output: Expected to contain "origin excluded (CN; baseOrigin=CN)"; Received "verifier alpha/m raised a candidate it would check".

members.title: Executable/chmodded text scripts still flagged as binary when not strict UTF-8 or containing ESC/other control chars
members.detail: The fix gates the mode condition on `reviewableText(bytes)`, which needs strict UTF-8 and rejects control bytes other than tab, newline, form feed and carriage return, instead of following the request (mode condition only for INERT_MEDIA_PATH). Git classifies these files as text (numstat counts lines), and the diff shows them like any other text. Even so, `binaryPaths` includes them, and the audit reports `binary bytes, such as a NUL`, which is false. This is the misleading diagnosis that cost run #376 three rounds, and the request explicitly says text files, executable or not, should be reviewed as text.

members.title: Allow unrelated skipped files when the requested test passed
members.detail: The global skippedFiles check rejects evidence even when the requested file passed without skips. This repository's full-suite gate intentionally skips Seatbelt tests inside confinement, so the reported loopback verification failure remains unresolved with its normal gate configuration. Targeted reproduction command: bun -e 'import { applyGateEvidence } from "./src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts"; import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; const sha="a".repeat(40); const result={ok:true,exitCode:0,output:"",testCoverage:{passedFiles:["test/loopback.test.ts"],skippedFiles:["test/sandbox.test.ts"],summary:{passed:1,failed:0}}}; const actual=applyGateEvidence({criteria:[{id:"AC-1",status:"blocked",blockedReason:"sandbox",evidence:"EPERM"}]},{acceptance_criteria:[{id:"AC-1",criterion:"tests pass",how_to_verify:"bun test test/loopback.test.ts"}]},{scenarios:[]},sha,{sha,stageId:12,checks:[{verdict:"pass",blocking:false,testCommand:"bun test",result}]}); assert.equal(actual.criteria[0].status,"met",actual.criteria[0].evidence);' Output: AssertionError: Factory gate substitution unavailable: candidate gate checks did not all pass cleanly without retries or skipped tests. 'blocked' !== 'met'.
members.failure_scenario: The candidate's bun test gate passes the loopback test but skips an unrelated Seatbelt-only test. The verifier cannot bind loopback and reports that targeted test blocked. Substitution refuses the passing evidence, and verification still ends as needs_human.

Consequently, an unrelated platform-specific skip prevents substitution even when the requested file ran and passed completely. This repository deliberately skips Seatbelt tests inside confined gates, so its normal suite cannot supply this evidence. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-gate-evidence.ts"`. Output: `{"mode":"unrelated-skip","gateOK":true,"coverage":{"passedFiles":["loopback.test.ts"],"skippedFiles":["actual.test.ts"],"summary":{"passed":1,"failed":0}},"status":"blocked"}`.
members.failure_scenario: The factory suite passes the required loopback test and skips an unrelated confinement test. The reader cannot bind loopback, so verification remains blocked and ultimately ends as needs_human despite the successful relevant gate result.

members.title: Unrelated skipped tests disable the fix in confined factory gates
members.detail: The clean-result guard rejects an entire gate if any file contains a skipped test, before checking coverage of the requested file. This repository deliberately skips real Seatbelt tests inside confined gates through seatbeltSkip, while its configured test gate runs the whole suite. A targeted applyGateEvidence probe with passedFiles ["test/loopback.test.ts"], skippedFiles ["test/sandbox.test.ts"], and a successful summary returned status "blocked" and "candidate gate checks did not all pass cleanly without retries or skipped tests." Thus even fully passing loopback tests in the normal factory suite cannot resolve the reported verification block.

members.title: Do not finalize pending results when another tool starts
members.detail: Calling reconcile(true) before every new call treats still-running calls as permanently missing results. Six parallel identical polls followed by an unrelated tool therefore abort the harness before their changing results arrive. Reproduction: `bun -e 'import { strict as a } from "node:assert"; import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) d.observe("shell", "poll", String(i)); a.equal(d.observe("Read", "file", "r"), null);'`. Output: `AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal: actual 'repeated the same shell call 6 times', expected null`.
members.failure_scenario: An assistant emits six identical shell calls and an unrelated Read in one parallel batch. The six shell results would all differ, but starting Read sets stuckReason and aborts before those results can clear the repetition count.

members.title: Do not finalize pending results when another tool call starts
members.detail: `observe()` calls `reconcile(true)` before registering every new call. Consequently, starting a seventh call treats six pending calls as a confirmed loop, although their eventual results may all differ. Both harnesses immediately abort on that reason. Reproduced with: bun -e 'import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); const reasons = []; for (let i = 0; i < 7; i++) reasons.push(d.observe("shell", "poll", String(i))); for (let i = 0; i < 7; i++) reasons.push(d.observeResult(String(i), `progress ${i}`)); console.log(JSON.stringify(reasons)); assert.equal(reasons.find(Boolean), undefined, "seven parallel calls with different results must not be classified as a loop");' Output: [null,null,null,null,null,null,"repeated the same shell call 6 times",null,null,null,null,null,null,null], followed by AssertionError.
members.failure_scenario: Claude emits seven identical tool_use blocks in one assistant message, or Codex emits seven identical command starts before completions. All results would differ, but the seventh start aborts the invocation before those results can establish progress.

members.title: An unrelated call prematurely finalizes pending results
members.detail: Every new call invokes reconcile(true), treating outstanding results as permanently missing. Five identical completed polls followed by a sixth pending poll and an unrelated Read therefore abort both harnesses before the sixth result can demonstrate progress. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100); for(let i=0;i<6;i++){d.observe("shell","poll",""+i);if(i<5)d.observeResult(""+i,"waiting");} console.log(d.observe("Read","file","r")); console.log(d.observeResult("5","progress"));' Output: "repeated the same shell call 6 times\nnull".
members.failure_scenario: Five polls return 'waiting'; the sixth poll starts alongside Read and would return 'progress'. Read's call event triggers cancellation before that changed result arrives.

members.title: Do not finalize pending results when another tool starts
members.detail: Every new call runs reconcile(true), treating pending results as permanently missing. After five unchanged polls and a pending sixth poll, an unrelated Read call therefore aborts both harnesses before the sixth poll can return changed output. Seven parallel identical calls likewise abort before any results arrive, even if every result would differ. Reproducer command: bun -e 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100); for(let i=0;i<5;i++){d.observe("shell","poll",String(i));d.observeResult(String(i),"waiting");} d.observe("shell","poll","5"); assert.equal(d.observe("Read","other.txt","read"),null); d.observeResult("5","progress");'. Output: AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION], actual 'repeated the same shell call 6 times', expected null.
members.failure_scenario: Five identical polls return 'waiting'; a sixth poll starts alongside an unrelated Read and would return 'progress'. The Read event causes an immediate stuck verdict before that changed result arrives.

members.title: Do not finalize pending calls when another tool starts
members.detail: Every new call runs reconcile(true), treating pending results as permanently missing. Six overlapping identical calls followed by an unrelated call therefore abort both harnesses before their differing results arrive. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector as D} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new D(100); for(let i=0;i<6;i++) d.observe("shell","poll",`${i}`); console.log(d.observe("Read","file","r")); for(let i=0;i<6;i++) d.observeResult(`${i}`,`${i}`); console.log(d.finish());' Output: `repeated the same shell call 6 times` followed by `null`. The harness aborts on the first output, so the later progress cannot rescue it.
members.failure_scenario: An assistant starts six identical polling calls and an unrelated Read before the polls return six different outputs.

members.title: Test output can forge coverage for a file that never ran
members.detail: The parser treats test-controlled console output as runner-generated file headers. A passing test that executes console.error("test/missing.test.ts:") causes its subsequent real passing row to be attributed to the nonexistent file. applyGateEvidence then marks a blocked criterion requiring that file as met. Reproduction command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-7zK26Q/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-7zK26Q/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-7zK26Q/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-7zK26Q/claude-501/review-gate-evidence.ts. Output: {"probe":"spoofed-header","missingExists":false,"actual":"met","expected":"blocked"}.
members.failure_scenario: An unrelated passing test prints the header of an absent or undiscovered required test. The verifier reports a sandbox block, and the engine substitutes fabricated coverage as authoritative factory evidence.

members.title: Test-controlled output can forge authoritative file coverage
members.detail: The parser treats arbitrary test stdout/stderr as runner-generated coverage. I ran `bun test` in a temporary directory containing only passing.test.ts, whose passing test printed `test/never-ran.test.ts:\n(pass) fabricated coverage`. The command exited 0 with `1 pass\n0 fail`; the parser recorded passedFiles=["test/never-ran.test.ts"], and applyGateEvidence changed the blocked criterion for that nonexistent file to `met` with factory provenance. This promotes output controlled by the change under test into authoritative verification evidence.
members.failure_scenario: A PR adds console output resembling Bun file headers and passing rows to an unrelated passing test. Broad gates pass, and a sandbox-blocked verification of a file that never ran receives a successful factory citation.

members.title: Test-written output can forge authoritative coverage
members.detail: The parser treats arbitrary test output as runner-owned file headers and passing rows. A real passing actual.test.ts printed `loopback.test.ts:\n(pass) fabricated loopback result`; loopback.test.ts did not exist. The engine nevertheless marked its blocked criterion met and attached factory provenance. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-gate-evidence.ts"`. Output: `{"mode":"spoof","gateOK":true,"coverage":{"passedFiles":["loopback.test.ts"],"skippedFiles":[],"summary":{"passed":1,"failed":0}},"status":"met"}`.
members.failure_scenario: A candidate test prints a forged header and passing row for an unexecuted required test. When the verifier reports that required test blocked by its sandbox, applyGateEvidence converts it to met.

members.title: Test-controlled output can forge factory coverage
members.detail: The parser treats arbitrary stdout and stderr as authoritative runner records. I ran `bun run -` with a temporary empty target.test.ts and an unrelated passing test that printed `target.test.ts:\n(pass) fabricated coverage`. The real runner reported `1 pass` across two files; parsed coverage included target.test.ts, and applyGateEvidence returned `"status":"met"` for the empty target. Thus implementer-controlled diagnostics become engine-owned proof that an unexecuted test passed.
members.failure_scenario: An unrelated passing test prints a required file's header and a fabricated passing row. The required file contains no tests, but a sandbox-blocked verification criterion becomes met with factory provenance.

members.title: Test-controlled output can forge factory coverage evidence

Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-gate-evidence.ts"` produced `{"scenario":"spoof","exitCode":0,"coverage":{"passedFiles":["loopback.test.ts"],"skippedFiles":[],"summary":{"passed":1,"failed":0}},"status":"met"...}`. members.title: Untrusted test output can forge factory coverage evidence
members.detail: The parser treats ordinary stdout/stderr as authoritative runner records. I ran `bun test` in a temporary directory containing only unrelated.test.ts, whose passing test executed `console.log("test/loopback.test.ts:\n(pass) loopback")`. Coverage reported passedFiles ["unrelated.test.ts", "test/loopback.test.ts"] and summary {passed:1,failed:0}. Feeding that result through applyGateEvidence returned status "met" with a factory citation for the nonexistent loopback file. Code under review can therefore fabricate coverage and bypass a blocked verification criterion.

members.title: Window eviction forgets the previous identical call's result
members.detail: Deleting results when a key leaves the window prevents comparison with the previous identical call, as required. After a gap, a changed result incorrectly counts as the first repetition. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100); d.observe("shell","poll","old"); d.observeResult("old","waiting"); for(let i=0;i<12;i++){d.observe("Read",i,"r"+i);d.observeResult("r"+i,"file");} for(let i=0;i<6;i++){console.log("call",i,d.observe("shell","poll","p"+i));console.log("result",i,d.observeResult("p"+i,"progress"));}' Output ends with "result 5 repeated the same shell call 6 times"; all earlier calls/results print null. The first 'progress' result differs from 'waiting' and should not count, leaving only five repetitions.
members.failure_scenario: A poll returns 'waiting', twelve other calls occur, then six polls return 'progress'. The detector stops one repetition too early.

members.title: Recover gate evidence consistently with the cached stage checkpoint
members.detail: RunContext.stage persists completedChecks and gateEvidence before marking the stage succeeded. A restart between those operations leaves a durable cached gate result whose stage is still running. On resume, the stage cache returns that result without rerunning gates or completing its stage record, while usableGates permanently rejects its evidence because the stage is not succeeded. A completed gate checkpoint therefore cannot support verification after this interruption.
members.failure_scenario: The daemon stops after the gates checkpoint save but before finishStage. The resumed run reuses cached checks, rejects their provenance, and sends an otherwise covered sandbox-blocked verification to needs_human.

members.title: Changed results reset counts but do not drop earlier occurrences
members.detail: Setting same = 0 leaves earlier occurrences in recent. Those discarded calls still consume window slots and prematurely evict other keys, contrary to the requested removal of earlier occurrences. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); for (let i=0;i<5;i++) d.observe("Read", "file"); d.observe("shell", "poll", "a"); d.observeResult("a", "A"); d.observe("shell", "poll", "b"); d.observeResult("b", "B"); for (let i=0;i<5;i++) d.observe("other", i); assert.equal(d.observe("Read", "file"), "repeated the same Read call 6 times");'. Output: AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal: actual null, expected 'repeated the same Read call 6 times'.
members.failure_scenario: Five identical Read calls, two poll calls producing A then B, five distinct calls, and a sixth identical Read call. The obsolete first poll remains in the window and causes the first Read to be evicted, so the detector misses the loop.

members.title: Exclude pre-reset pending calls from result deferral
members.detail: Changed output resets the count but leaves earlier pending entries in recent. The pending-entry check includes those discarded occurrences and suppresses detection even after six subsequent calls complete with identical results. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector as D} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new D(100); d.observe("shell","poll","missing"); for(let i=0;i<8;i++){d.observe("shell","poll",`${i}`); console.log(d.observeResult(`${i}`,i===0?"A":"B"));} console.log(d.finish());' Output: eight `null` lines, then `repeated the same shell call 6 times`. The sixth unchanged B result should already report the loop.
members.failure_scenario: One old poll never returns; later output changes from A to B, followed by six completed B results. Detection waits for another call or invocation termination instead of stopping on the sixth unchanged result.

members.title: --ignore-case misses Unicode case equivalents
members.detail: Lowercasing is not Unicode case folding. Greek uppercase sigma lowercases contextually, so lines differing only in case can retain different keys. Command: bun -e 'import { run } from "./src/cli.ts"; const actual = run(["dedupe", "--ignore-case", "ΟΣ\nοσ"]); console.log(JSON.stringify(actual)); if (actual !== "ΟΣ") throw new Error("Expected only the first line: ΟΣ");'. Output: "ΟΣ\nοσ", followed by 'error: Expected only the first line: ΟΣ' (exit 1). This contradicts the documented case-insensitive behavior.
members.failure_scenario: Run dedupe --ignore-case with the two lines ΟΣ and οσ. Both survive despite differing only in case.

members.title: Lowercasing misses Unicode case-equivalent duplicates
members.detail: Lowercasing is not Unicode case folding: capital sigma Σ becomes σ, while lowercase final sigma ς remains distinct. The command `bun src/cli.ts dedupe --ignore-case $'Σ\nς'` outputs `Σ\nς` instead of retaining only `Σ`, contradicting the documented case-insensitive behavior.
members.failure_scenario: Input contains Σ and ς on separate lines with --ignore-case enabled; both lines survive.

members.title: Trailing line terminators create a phantom blank output line
members.detail: Splitting newline-terminated text retains a trailing empty element. The CLI then adds another newline through console.log(), introducing a blank line absent from the input. Command: `bun src/cli.ts dedupe $'a\na\n' | od -An -tx1`. Output: `61 0a 0a`; expected `61 0a`.
members.failure_scenario: Running dedupe on two newline-terminated copies of `a` prints `a` followed by an additional blank line.

members.title: Lowercasing does not provide Unicode caseless matching
members.detail: Greek capital sigma and final sigma are case variants but lowercase to different strings, so --ignore-case retains both. Command: `bun -e 'import {run} from "./src/cli.ts"; console.log(JSON.stringify(run(["dedupe", "--ignore-case", "Σ\nς"])));'`. Output: `"Σ\nς"`; expected `"Σ"`.
members.failure_scenario: Input `Σ\nς` with --ignore-case retains duplicate case variants despite the documented behavior.
